title: Jefferies Keeps Buy Ratings on Six Adani Stocks, Backs $51 Billion Capex Plan
excerpt: The brokerage reaffirmed Buys across the Adani Group, set target prices for all six names, and projected 23% compound EBITDA and EPS growth through FY29 — while flagging leverage and execution risk.
body:
• Jefferies has reaffirmed Buy ratings on all six Adani Group companies it covers, calling the group a "hard-asset play" built on infrastructure with predictable cash flows.
  • The brokerage expects the group's combined EBITDA and earnings per share to grow at a 23% compound annual rate between FY26 and FY29 — a projection, not a result.
  • Target prices: Adani Enterprises ₹3,830, Adani Ports ₹2,180, Adani Power ₹240, Adani Green Energy ₹1,695, Adani Energy Solutions ₹1,980 and Ambuja Cements ₹475.
  • The bull case rests on roughly $51 billion of planned capital spending between FY27 and FY29; Jefferies itself flags elevated leverage at some group entities and execution risk on that programme.

Jefferies has reaffirmed its bullish stance on the Adani Group, maintaining Buy ratings across all six companies under its coverage and describing the conglomerate as a hard-asset play — a portfolio weighted toward physical infrastructure rather than cyclical or discretionary businesses. In the note reported Monday, the brokerage cited robust earnings visibility, a strong investment pipeline and growing exposure to infrastructure businesses with predictable cash flows.

The ratings and targets

"Jefferies said over 65% of the group's funds from operations are expected to come from businesses with predictable cash flows, which it argues improves earnings stability and visibility."

Jefferies retained Buy calls on Adani Enterprises, Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone, Adani Power, Adani Green Energy, Adani Energy Solutions and Ambuja Cements, with target prices of ₹3,830, ₹2,180, ₹240, ₹1,695, ₹1,980 and ₹475 respectively. The brokerage expects the group's combined EBITDA and earnings per share to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 23% between FY26 and FY29, driven by capacity expansions, market-share gains and the commissioning of new projects. Those growth figures are Jefferies' forecasts, and they depend on the investment programme below being delivered on schedule.

A $51 billion capex programme anchors the case

According to Jefferies, the group plans capital investments of about $51 billion between FY27 and FY29 — nearly 28% of the total planned capital expenditure by major Indian conglomerates, and more than one-fifth of what major business groups plan to spend. More than half of the planned outlay is directed toward power utilities, deepening the group's exposure to regulated and contracted infrastructure. Jefferies said over 65% of the group's funds from operations are expected to come from businesses with predictable cash flows, which it argues improves earnings stability and visibility.

The operating footprint behind the note is substantial. Adani Ports remains India's largest private port operator with a 27% market share. Adani Power and Adani Green Energy together account for roughly 7% of India's installed power-generation capacity. Adani Airports handles approximately 23% of the country's passenger traffic, with the upcoming Navi Mumbai Airport expected to serve as a long-term growth catalyst. Adani Enterprises, the group's incubation vehicle, houses emerging businesses spanning airports, data centres, green hydrogen, solar manufacturing, copper processing and defence — the segment where Jefferies sees substantial long-term value. The full wire report is carried by Nation Press and Bilkul Bazaar.

The risks Jefferies itself flags

The note is not unqualified. Jefferies' analysts flagged elevated leverage at certain group entities, execution challenges associated with the scale of the capital expenditure programme, and interconnected exposures across companies that could amplify stress during adverse market conditions. With project commissioning set to ramp up through FY29, the pace of execution and the group's ability to maintain funding access are the variables the market will watch — the same variables the 23% growth projection depends on.
